To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy demand of the UV photodegradation post-process was lowest at low organic loading rate (olrad), and the bioenergy produced from the anaerobic digestion process could supply energy to meet the photodegradation energy demand.
the bioenergy from AD can be used to power the energy-intensive photoreactor to achieve a sustainable process for treating distillery effluents.
the integrated anaerobic photodegradation process has the potential to reduce carbon emission and is sustainable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a sustainable treatment process for distillery wastewater in which bioenergy from the biological step is used to power the energy-intensive photolysis step.
the modelling of the integrated AD and UV photodegradation of the distillery effluent with a view of achieving energy sustainability and environmental conservation.
the development of a sustainable AD and photodegradation process for distillery wastewater treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy demand of the UV photodegradation step could be reduced by 93% when the biological step is operated at OLR AD of 3  kg COD/m3  d and HRT of AD of 20 days, thus making the process energy efficient.
AD and photodegradation are effective in organic removal and colour removal, respectively, and the energy produced from the biological step is sufficient for powering the photodegradation step.
a sustainable process could be developed in which bioenergy production from AD could be used to power the photodegradation step for colour removal from distillery effluent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed integrated AD and UV photodegradation of the distillery effluent would be an efficient, sustainable and environmentally friendly process for bioenergy production, energy demand reduction and environmental conservation.
the integrated AD and photodegradation system is energy-efficient and environmentally friendly.
the energy efficiency of the proposed integrated system was improved by about 31%, which is a significant improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AD of distillery effluents could supply energy to power the photodegradation post treatment.
AD of distillery effluents can produce enough bioenergy to supply the photodegradation energy demand and hence reduce carbon emission.
the biological step can supply energy for the photodegradation process, which is energy intensive, thus making the overall system sustainable.
